items.text: Unofficial Nov 3 returns showed Pataskala and Granville, Ohio, voters backing charter amendments to restrict large data centers. Other communities rejected development proposals or backed restrictions.
items.context: Citizen initiatives put zoning limits directly to voters. Ohio Municipal League distinguishes rejected development proposals from advisory votes. Track certification, effective dates and project exposure by jurisdiction. https://www.boe.ohio.gov/licking/election-info/election-results/ https://omlohio.org/m/newsflash/Home/Detail/59
items.source: Axios Columbus; Licking County results index; Ohio Municipal League
items.rationale: My reading: local voters used the ballot to constrain where developers can build, raising permitting and relocation risks for capital-intensive projects. Developers with approvals elsewhere may gain a relative advantage. Federal preemption and nationwide capacity effects remain open.
items.fxnote: No fx: preliminary local votes establish siting pressure, with federal faction leverage and project-level losses still unmeasured.
items.precedent: Earlier 2026 municipal data-center votes tested local siting authority. This set spans more jurisdictions and includes advisory questions as well as charter amendments.

challenge.reading: Local restrictions can redirect investment toward already-permitted sites. Verify the local legal effect and project exposure before inferring an aggregate capacity loss.

items.actor: Nvidia board; Jensen Huang; Marco Rubio
items.text: Nvidia’s board opens an inquiry into reports that foreign intelligence targeted chief executive Jensen Huang.
items.context: Nvidia’s November 8 statement assigns the inquiry to independent directors and outside counsel. The board continues to support chief executive Jensen Huang and says it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised. The inquiry is a new corporate action following the October 29 reports alleging that Megaspeed, a chip buyer, was involved in diversion to China, not a finding that espionage occurred. On November 9, Anadolu relayed a New York Times report that Secretary of State Marco Rubio supervised a warning memo in spring. The classified memo was not available for this review; that account remains attributed reporting. My reading: the inquiry gives officials seeking tighter chip-export controls a fresh reason to demand answers, but neither an export restriction nor a gain in Rubio’s primary support has been established. https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/rubio-oversaw-classified-memo-alleging-nvidia-ceo-s-ties-to-suspected-chinese-intelligence-operative-report/4116377
items.rationale: My reading: corporate oversight can expose information relevant to chip controls, while the executive branch and Congress retain separate policy powers.
items.fxnote: No fx: this development establishes a statement or review, not a demonstrated change in a tracked faction’s control of policy.

items.text: Minneapolis lists a November 12 council meeting on proposed data-center zoning.
items.context: The city describes a temporary pause on most new proposals and proposed rules on location, size, noise and resource reporting. Its page lists the November 12 meeting but carries an October 16 update label. My reading: local land-use authority can constrain construction even when federal officials favor investment. The page does not establish final adoption or a decision about electricity prices.
items.rationale: My reading: local land-use authority can constrain construction even when federal officials favor investment. The page does not establish final adoption or a decision about electricity prices.
items.fxnote: No change assigned to faction authority: the record identifies a pending local decision, not a final restriction or a shift in federal control.

items.actor: Howard Lutnick, Scott Bessent and Marco Rubio
items.text: Axios reports Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick delayed controls on suspected Nvidia chip diversions to China
items.context: Axios cited six sources briefed on or familiar with the discussions. They said President Trump authorized action repeatedly and the Commerce Department held back. Commerce denied Axios’s account of a confrontation between Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Lutnick. The reported discussions included Secretary of State Marco Rubio. An operative restriction and the outcome of Nvidia’s separate board inquiry remain unverified.
items.rationale: My reading: The account suggests Commerce can delay implementation even when senior officials seek restrictions. The president can still settle the dispute. The report leaves the reasons for delay and the suspected diversion open.
items.fxnote: No fx: The reported deliberations leave the final Commerce decision open.
